pillars.label: Customer health
pillars.meaning: Share of baseline order value held by accounts with no elevated-or-worse risk.
pillars.implication: A drop means more of the business sits with customers showing a multi-signal risk pattern.

pillars.label: Supply continuity
pillars.meaning: Portfolio fill rate over the last 4 weeks: units shipped / units ordered.
pillars.implication: Below the high-90s usually means a supply-side problem we caused, not demand.

pillars.label: Service quality
pillars.meaning: Share of support tickets answered within the 8-hour SLA in the last 4 weeks.
pillars.implication: Falling SLA compliance makes supply problems feel like neglect to customers.

pillars.label: Field coverage
pillars.meaning: Touchpoints in the last 4 weeks vs the portfolio's normal 4-week level (capped at 100).
pillars.implication: Relationships fade quietly before orders fall.

pillars.label: Commercial momentum
pillars.meaning: 50 + percentage change in seasonality-adjusted units vs the normal 4-week level.
pillars.implication: Above 50 means growing after seasonality; below 50 means shrinking.

catalog.label: Order volume
catalog.definition: Units ordered, last 4 weeks vs baseline weekly mean x 4, as fractional change.
catalog.caption: How much less (or more) this account bought recently than its own normal. A drop alone is weak; a drop with other signals is a pattern.

catalog.label: Order value
catalog.definition: Order value (INR), same windows as order_volume_delta.
catalog.caption: Same idea as volume but in rupees, so a mix shift to cheaper products shows up.

catalog.label: reorder_interval_drift
catalog.definition: For chronic-therapy SKUs only: median days between reorders, last 8 weeks vs baseline. Positive = reordering later.
catalog.caption: Patients on chronic therapy need steady refills. When a pharmacy reorders later than usual, patients may be missing doses or switching brands.

catalog.label: Growth with product gap
catalog.definition: Order volume growth for an account in >=2 therapy areas while a complementary therapy area has near-zero purchase.
catalog.caption: This account is growing fast in related products but does not buy a complementary one. That gap is a sales opportunity.

catalog.label: Fill rate
catalog.definition: sum(qty_filled)/sum(qty_ordered), last 4 weeks. Compared to baseline fill rate.
catalog.caption: Share of what the customer asked for that we actually shipped. Falling fill rate usually means a supply problem on our side, not a demand problem on theirs.

catalog.label: Delivery delay
catalog.definition: Mean (delivered_date - promised_date) in days, last 4 weeks.
catalog.caption: Average lateness against what we promised. Customers feel this before they complain.

catalog.label: Stock cover
catalog.definition: warehouse on_hand / trailing 4-week mean daily dispatch, per SKU.
catalog.caption: How many days of this product the warehouse can still ship. Under about a week it becomes the likely cause of downstream customer problems.

catalog.label: Supplier ETA slips
catalog.definition: Number of times inbound_eta has moved later in the last 28 days.
catalog.caption: Each slip of the supplier's promised arrival date is evidence of a supplier or manufacturing delay.

catalog.label: Complaints
catalog.definition: Count of complaints (kinds: service, delivery, billing) in the last 4 weeks vs baseline. COUNT, not rate: this is what deck slide 7 shows ('Complaints up 47%').
catalog.caption: How many more complaints this account raised than it normally does in four weeks. Note that fewer orders with more complaints means the experience got worse, not just busier.

catalog.label: Response time
catalog.definition: Median (first_response_at - opened_at), last 4 weeks vs baseline.
catalog.caption: How much slower we are answering this account. Slow replies make a supply problem feel like neglect.

catalog.label: Regional SLA breaches
catalog.definition: Open tickets older than SLA per 100 tickets, by region.
catalog.caption: When many accounts in one region get slower at once, the cause is support capacity, not individual customers.

catalog.label: Touchpoints
catalog.definition: Visits+calls+WhatsApp touchpoints per 4 weeks vs baseline.
catalog.caption: How much less we are in touch with this account. Relationships fade quietly before orders fall.

catalog.label: Nephrologist visit gap
catalog.definition: Days since last rep visit to a nephrologist linked to a hospital/clinic account, vs that prescriber's usual cadence.
catalog.caption: Doctors who stop being visited tend to prescribe less over time. This catches the gap early.

catalog.label: Rep coverage
catalog.definition: Active reps / accounts per region vs the portfolio norm.
catalog.caption: Accounts per rep. When a rep leaves, every account they covered starts to drift.

catalog.label: Overdue receivables
catalog.definition: Overdue (>0 days past due) outstanding / trailing 12-week billing.
catalog.caption: How much of what this account owes us is late. Paired with falling orders it suggests the customer is under financial stress.

catalog.label: Batch complaint cluster
catalog.definition: Quality-kind complaints for the same batch_id from >=2 distinct accounts within 21 days.
catalog.caption: Several customers complaining about the same batch is a quality pattern. Strata routes it to the QA head and never acts on it automatically.

catalog.label: Possible adverse-event report
catalog.definition: Complaint text classified as possible adverse-event report (keyword + classifier-lite). Routing flag only, not a medical judgement.
catalog.caption: A complaint that might describe a patient reaction. Strata only makes sure a human on the QA side sees it; it makes no medical decision.

catalog.label: expiry_exposure_value
catalog.definition: INR value of channel stock expiring within 90 days where trailing sell-through implies it will not clear.
catalog.caption: Stock sitting at a customer that will probably expire before it sells. This becomes returns and credit notes unless moved.

catalog.caption: Repeated rows can look like a sudden spike in orders. A high value means the data, not the customer, changed.

items.title: Hospital pharmacy short-shipped after phosphate binder supplier slip
items.body: A contract manufacturer pushed back two consecutive dispatches of a phosphate binder SKU. The hospital pharmacy at Fictiva General received partial deliveries for several weeks. The issue surfaced through repeated ETA revisions rather than through the account itself. We learned to watch ETA slips as an early warning before fill rate visibly drops.

steps.action: Split available stock pro rata across affected hospital accounts
Escalate to supplier and obtain a committed dispatch date
Share the revised ETA with the pharmacy purchase lead

items.resolution: Split remaining stock across hospital accounts pro rata, escalate supplier, share revised ETA with pharmacy

items.title: Chemist chain switched source during prolonged supplier delay
items.body: An active ingredient shortage at an upstream supplier delayed a chronic CKD SKU for over a month. The Kestrel Pharmacies chain was not contacted until its orders had already stopped. By the time stock returned, the chain had moved the line to an alternative source. The lesson was that silence during a delay costs more than the delay itself.

steps.action: Restore supply once supplier dispatch arrived
Visit the chain buyer to request reinstatement of the line

items.resolution: Late outreach after stock returned; no interim supply offered

items.title: Nephrology clinic orders paused during iron supplement supplier delay
items.body: A packaging line breakdown at a supplier delayed an oral iron supplement SKU. The Riverbend Kidney Clinic paused orders and logged a delivery complaint. Operations noticed the low stock cover at the regional warehouse a few days late. Supply recovered, but the clinic reduced its standing order for the following quarter.

steps.action: Escalate supplier and confirm repair timeline
Release part of the regional buffer to the clinic
Call the clinic with the revised ETA

items.resolution: Escalate supplier, contact clinic with revised ETA, partial reallocation from regional buffer

items.title: Stockist ran dry on a high-velocity renal SKU before month-end
items.body: A regional stockist under-ordered ahead of a holiday period and ran out of a high-velocity SKU. Downstream chemists began reporting unavailability through field reps. Our warehouse had stock; the gap was in the channel, not upstream. An expedited replenishment closed the gap within days.

steps.action: Raise an expedited dispatch from the nearest warehouse
Agree a minimum holding norm with the stockist
Inform field reps that stock is restored

items.resolution: Expedite replenishment from warehouse, agree a minimum stock norm with the stockist

items.title: Chemist chain outlets out of stock after central DC transfer delay
items.body: The Northgate Chemists central distribution centre delayed inter-store transfers during a system migration. Several outlets showed empty shelves while the chain's central stock was healthy. We noticed via a dip in outlet-level orders routed through the stockist. Direct-to-outlet dispatch for a short window bridged the gap.

steps.action: Identify affected outlets with the chain logistics lead
Arrange temporary direct dispatch to those outlets
Confirm normal transfers resumed before stopping direct dispatch

items.resolution: Temporary direct dispatch to affected outlets, coordinate with chain logistics

items.title: Hospital pharmacy stockout from missed tender call-off
items.body: The hospital pharmacy at Lakeview Medical Centre missed a scheduled call-off under its annual tender. Pharmacy stock ran low before anyone on either side noticed. The reorder interval had been drifting for weeks, which was the earliest sign. The account was recovered but the procurement relationship was strained.

steps.action: Process an emergency call-off against the tender
Agree a reorder reminder cadence with hospital procurement

items.resolution: Emergency call-off processed, reorder reminder cadence agreed with procurement

items.title: Warehouse system showed stock that was physically unavailable
items.body: Orders from a stockist were confirmed against system stock that turned out to be quarantined. Dispatches were short and the stockist was given inaccurate ETAs. A cycle count revealed the quarantine flag had not synced to the order system. The sync rule was fixed and the stockist was given priority dispatch.

steps.action: Run a cycle count on the affected SKU locations
Correct the quarantine status sync with the IT team
Give the stockist a corrected ETA and priority dispatch

items.resolution: Cycle count, fix quarantine sync, priority dispatch to affected stockist

items.title: Near-expiry stock stranded at one depot while another ran short
items.body: One depot held a large lot approaching expiry while a neighbouring depot could not fill chain orders. The imbalance was visible only when expiry exposure was reviewed at month-end.
